lead: # The plan is the input: repos, issues (with their GitHub identity), and fleet streams.
# The transport, extracted so this crate can exist at all.
# Publish a plan's GitHub structure with no frontend involved
# It lives in its OWN crate rather than under `bsc plan` because `bsc plan` routes wholly into
# `plandb`, a store crate with no networking — putting reqwest + TLS behind a SQLite store would be
# a layering inversion, and depending the other way (plandb -> publish -> plandb) is a cycle. So
# publish sits ABOVE both stores and the transport, and `bsc` dispatches to it directly.
sections.name: [dependencies]

lead: # build.rs parses the committed graph store directly — see crates/graph-materialize/build.rs.
# THE SHARED CRATE ROOT — this crate owns no source file at all. See
# crates/graph-materialize/crate_root.rs; the crate's own docs come from its record.
# THE TEST SOURCES ARE IN THE GRAPH, not in this directory
# `tests/idempotency.rs` exists: each whole file is an EDGE in graph/algorithms.json
# (`bsc-publish--board-adoption`, `bsc-publish--idempotency`), which also records the member records
# it spans. The shared build script materializes each into `$OUT_DIR/tests/<name>.rs` and the shared
# root below `include!`s the one named by `CARGO_CRATE_NAME` — which is the TARGET's name, so both
# entries point at ONE file and each still resolves its own body.
sections.name: [[test]]
